title: The Gut Resistome Atlas in Preterm Infants Enables Prediction of Necrotizing Enterocolitis Onset.
summary: Machine-learning analysis of preterm-infant gut resistomes identified convergence before necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) onset. A random-forest model achieved external-cohort AUROC 0.823 versus 0.727 for bacterial-species features; the external evaluation included only nine NEC cases and 16 controls, so this is an early predictive association, not clinical readiness or causation.
ai_technology: A 500-tree random forest uses gut-resistome features to predict impending NEC.
organization: West China Second University Hospital, Sichuan University; Guangzhou Women and Children’s Medical Center; Zhujiang Hospital, Southern Medical University

evidence.tested: The study reports resistome convergence before NEC onset and external-validation AUROC 0.823, compared with 0.727 for bacterial-species features.
evidence.unknown: The external cohort contains 9 NEC cases and 16 controls; the study does not establish causation or clinical readiness.
evidence.ai_role: A random-forest model links infant gut resistome profiles to the reported NEC early-warning result.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
